forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Rochford's accounts disclaimed by auditors for four years running; council debt-free and £500k ahead on interest
news_drafts.lead:
Rochford District Council's accounts for 2021/22, 2022/23, 2023/24 and 2024/25 have all been disclaimed by its external auditor, Ernst & Young (EY), meaning the auditor could not fully sign off the accounts (a "disclaimer" is stronger than a qualified opinion). The Audit, Governance and Standards Committee on 5 October has an addendum to the audit plan saying assurance "has not been obtained over the brought-forward balances and some of the movements during the disclaimed periods."

EY's risk assessment says the gaps before 2023/24, particularly in reserves (money the council has put aside) and other cumulative balances, "cannot be sufficiently addressed as part of the 2025/26 audit." It says it will focus on bodies that have shown they can support all planned 2025/26 audit procedures. The council's own paper says progress is behind the expected timescales for rebuilding assurance because the disclaimer period covers three years. The papers say external valuers could not provide suitable supporting evidence for property valuations in 2023/24 and 2024/25. The 2024/25 audit has begun rebuilding assurance, with property, plant and equipment the focus for 2025/26.

The treasury management report (how the council borrows and invests its cash) for the first quarter of 2026/27 is more positive. The council stayed debt-free and took no external borrowing. Interest income is forecast at £1.1m against a £600k budget, which the council attributes to higher opening cash balances after a stronger 2025/26 outturn (the actual figures once the year had ended) and to capital programme slippage that keeps money invested longer. Capital spending, on things that last, is forecast at £11.236m against £11.652m, an underspend of £416k, mainly from the Rochford Town Centre Project. That cuts the planned use of the council's own cash to pay for capital spending (internal borrowing) from £4.4m to £3.984m.

Internal audit's first-quarter update lists four medium-priority recommendations overdue after missing three to five implementation dates, covering overtime, travel and subsistence, policy framework training and debt recovery tools. Management blames "high volume of workload and capacity with the team." Two procurement actions have moved from 4 June to 1 November 2026. Budget-holder analytics are now live.

findings.headline: Eight of 10 recent audit recommendations have been fully implemented and closed.
findings.detail: Of 10 high and medium priority recommendations reviewed by BDO, eight have been fully implemented and closed. Completed recommendations span Member Enquiries, Corporate Governance, Cyber Security in the Supply Chain, Procurement and Contract Management, and Project Management. Two remain in progress with agreed revised implementation dates. This shows the council is largely responsive to audit findings across a range of governance and operational areas.
findings.matters: Strong implementation rates on audit recommendations indicate the council is taking assurance seriously and is responsive to identified control weaknesses, reducing governance risk.
findings.figures: 8 of 10 high and medium priority recommendations fully implemented and closed.
findings.quote: Of these, eight recommendations have been fully implemented and closed, while the remaining recommendations are still being progressed.

findings.headline: Internal audit function not in full conformity with external quality assessment standards.
findings.detail: The Internal Audit function is in full conformity with eight of nine Global Internal Audit Standards Essential Conditions, but does not fully conform with Standard 8.4 on External Quality Assessment. The council does not approve the scope, frequency, assessor competencies or action plans for external quality assessments conducted by BDO. An alternative arrangement is proposed whereby the Committee will receive information on scope and outcomes of future external assessments.
findings.matters: A governance gap in external audit oversight reduces council control over how its audit function is independently assessed, which could be relevant to peers evaluating controls and to lenders assessing governance risk.
findings.figures: 8 of 9 Essential Conditions in full conformity; 1 of 9 assessed as 'Generally Conforms'.
findings.quote: While BDO undergoes an independent External Quality Assessment every five years across its internal audit service, the Council does not directly approve the scope, frequency, assessor competencies or any resulting action plans, as required under the Essential Conditions.

findings.headline: Four audit recommendations remain overdue due to workload, capacity pressures, unsuccessful recruitment, and system implementation delays.
findings.detail: Of 10 reviewed high and medium priority recommendations, four remain overdue: two from Overtime and Expenses audit citing workload and capacity pressures (revised 31 October 2026), one from Policy Framework audit delayed by unsuccessful recruitment to a permanent post (revised 30 September 2026, though multiple previous date revisions raise credibility concerns), and one from Debt Recovery audit delayed by system implementation prerequisites (anticipated end of Q2 2026/27). The pattern of overdue recommendations indicates operational constraints affecting the council's ability to implement its own audit-directed improvements.
findings.matters: Overdue audit recommendations citing capacity and recruitment problems indicate operational constraints that could affect the council's ability to implement other critical changes and suggest underlying staffing or resource issues.
findings.figures: Four of 10 reviewed high and medium priority recommendations classified as overdue. Revised implementation dates: 31 October 2026, 30 September 2026, end of Q2 2026/27.
findings.quote: Two medium-priority recommendations from the Overtime and Expenses audit remain overdue. These relate to the development of an Overtime Policy and a Travel and Subsistence Policy. Both recommendations have experienced delays due to workload and capacity pressures.

findings.paper_title: Reserve Risk Assessment update report (Audit plan addendum)
findings.headline: The majority of English district councils received disclaimed audit opinions for 2024/25, with assurance gaps in reserves, property plant and equipment, and income and expenditure common across the sector.
findings.detail: This is a sector-wide issue affecting most district councils, not unique to Rochford. However, Rochford's relative positioning in Quartile 1 indicates the council is handling these sector pressures better than most peers, despite the disclaimer opinion.
findings.matters: A peer finance director can understand this is a structural sector issue requiring multi-year attention; a lender can see Rochford is managing these common pressures better than most peers, which informs relative credit assessment
findings.quote: The majority of district councils received disclaimed audit opinions for 2024/25, with assurance gaps over reserves, property, plant and equipment, and income and expenditure common across the sector.

findings.paper_title: Reserve Risk Assessment update report (Audit plan addendum)
findings.headline: EY will seek a fee variation to cover the cost of reserve risk assessment work and historic assurance rebuilding procedures, outside the scale fee agreed in April 2026.
findings.detail: The reserve risk assessment, MHCLG submission preparation, and procedures for rebuilding historic assurance fall outside the baseline scale fee set by EY's April 2026 Audit Planning Report. The variation will be negotiated and communicated once agreed. The 2024/25 audit required a fee variation of £28,580, providing a reference point for potential costs.
findings.matters: Audit fee variations signal expanded scope and additional costs; knowing a prior-year variation was £28,580 helps the council estimate potential 2025/26 costs and indicates the quantum of additional audit work required
findings.quote: In addition, procedures relating to the rebuilding of historical assurance will also be outside the scale fee. Accordingly, EY will seek a variation to the scale fee to reflect these changes to the scope of their work
